hypothesis: Two margins rank the routes differently. The focus margin s_c - L (T024: first conjugate point, a zero of j_head, minus the route length) is positive for every candidate route, so each is locally length minimizing to the edge; the focal clearance ratio (nearest zero of j_lat or j_head over L) separates them and ranks routes differently from length: the straight route over the dome is the shortest candidate route to the far edge yet has a focal point of lateral offsets inside it.
input_data: Fan of geodesic routes (T136) at h = 1 and 2 mm; horizon 2.5 x the chart reach
Routes at 1 and 2 deg for the second variation
mathematical_model: Conjugate points: zeros of j_head (s > 0); focal points: zeros of j_lat. Focus margin = s_c - L, recorded as no value when censored (no conjugate point within the horizon), with the lower bound horizon - L kept separately; focal clearance ratio = s_focus / L with s_focus the nearest focal or conjugate point, or horizon / L as a lower bound; L''(0) = j_head(L) j_head'(L) for routes from a point to a straight edge line.
numerical_result: focus margin: {fan+0deg, fan+10deg, fan+15deg, fan+20deg, fan+25deg, fan+5deg} (no conjugate point within the horizon: lower bounds, tied), censored margins (no value) with lower bounds from 297.8 mm (min j_head(s) / s = 0.534); focal clearance ratio: {fan+15deg, fan+20deg, fan+25deg} (no focus within the horizon: lower bounds, tied) > fan+10deg > fan+5deg > fan+0deg; shortest fan+0deg (202.1797 mm) has ratio 0.759 with a focal point at 153.41 mm and focus margin >= 297.8 mm (censored); L''(0) finite difference 36.9633 mm vs index form 36.9639 mm.
observation_model: No observation: margins and lengths are model outputs.

title: Rank paths by focus margin.
uncertainty: Focus locations agree to 2.9e-04 mm and route lengths to 4.9e-06 mm between step sizes; lower-bound margins and ratios depend on the horizon.
unresolved_assumptions: No candidate route has a conjugate point within 2.5 x its reach, so the focus margin only bounds them from below and ties them; the focal clearance ratio, which includes zeros of j_lat, is the quantity that ranks.

The straight route is a local length minimum (L'' > 0, positive focus margin) although it contains a lateral focal point; a focal point of the start normal does not contradict minimality to the edge line.
The fan is a discrete candidate set; margins between sampled headings are not bounded.
